title: CompliHub360 approved wizard design
status: Approved question design; production dependencies remain open

groups.title: Shared questions
groups.purpose: Build a short, reusable profile, then ask only the category questions that can change the requested service or Provider fit.
notes: Ask shared facts once. Confirm reuse only for the same entity, work, countries and product group. A multi-category user does not repeat the shared interview.

Country, language and local-form catalogues are selection controls, not free-text fields. Exact catalogue content is maintained separately. The flashcards show the control specification rather than an incomplete global list.
Personal matter is an approved design option but remains on hold for launch until platform scope and Terms are resolved. Do not place that user into a business journey by default.
No generic start-date, budget, company size or motivation question is added. Use a deadline only for work affected by a real date.

cards.prompt: Which best describes your situation?
cards.why: Separates existing operations, planned activity and the unresolved personal-user scope.
cards.when: First card.
cards.notes: Personal matter must not launch before the scope decision. Not sure triggers short factual clarification, not an invented company.

cards.prompt: What brings you here today?
cards.why: Distinguishes a launch, transfer, ongoing service and active issue so follow-ups fit the actual task.
cards.when: Once per relevant project.
cards.notes: Not sure is exclusive. Map changing Provider to the affected work later; it does not mean a problem occurred.

cards.prompt: Where is your business established?
options: Country selector: six regions on the same card; choose countries or territories without typing.
cards.why: Keeps the business home location separate from sales markets and service jurisdictions.
cards.when: Existing business, or formation status is relevant.
cards.notes: If not established, show planned establishment countries / Still deciding inline. Never derive this from the first sales market.

cards.prompt: What do you sell or provide?
cards.why: Avoids stock and product branches for users who only provide services.
cards.when: Business activity is relevant.
cards.notes: Still deciding and Not sure are each exclusive.

cards.prompt: Who do you sell to?
cards.why: Separates consumer-facing work from business sales without asking users to interpret legal duties.
cards.when: Sales context affects the selected work.

cards.prompt: How do you sell or provide your offering?
cards.why: Distinguishes marketplace sellers from platform operators and identifies relevant channels.
cards.when: Channel affects the selected work.
cards.notes: Still deciding and Not sure are each exclusive. A seller is not automatically a marketplace operator.

cards.prompt: Which countries do you sell to?
options: Country selector: six regions on the same card; choose countries or territories without typing.
cards.why: Records actual customer markets without treating planned markets as existing sales.
cards.when: Markets affect the selected work.
cards.notes: Show planned markets inline when needed, with Still deciding. Preserve separate current and planned fields.

cards.prompt: Where do you hold stock?
options: Country selector: six regions on the same card; choose countries or territories without typing.
cards.why: Identifies stock locations that may matter independently of customer countries.
cards.when: Physical products and stock location affects the selected work.
cards.notes: Include fulfilment and marketplace warehouses. Prelaunch wording: Where will you hold stock? Choices include No stock will be held and Still deciding.

cards.prompt: How is this work currently handled?
cards.why: Supports new work, supplementary help and a Provider transfer without assuming a service failure.
cards.when: Existing arrangements for the selected work are unknown.
cards.notes: Different arrangements opens inline rows by service and country. Never apply one answer to all categories without confirmation.

cards.prompt: Which languages are you comfortable using for support?
options: Language selector: choose from the maintained language catalogue without typing.
cards.why: Finds a mutually usable support language without requiring every selected language.
cards.when: Once; reuse across categories unless the user changes it.
cards.notes: Any selected language is acceptable. Unconfirmed Provider language is not a verified match. Content translation languages are separate.

cards.prompt: How would you prefer to communicate?
cards.why: Adds a useful preference without excluding a qualified Provider for an unverified communication channel.
cards.when: Once; optional preference.
cards.notes: No preference is exclusive. Treat as a soft preference and confirm actual availability before booking.

cards.prompt: What do you need help with?
options: Help me identify what I need
cards.why: Routes directly to relevant category questions and provides a guided route when the user cannot name the service.
cards.when: Once after enough context to route; do not force irrelevant shared facts first.
cards.notes: Help me identify what I need is exclusive. Suggest topics from factual context and ask the user to confirm them; do not mark obligations confirmed.

cards.prompt: Is there a deadline for this work?
cards.why: Captures a real constraint for an issue, filing or time-sensitive appointment without asking everyone about urgency.
cards.when: A selected issue or service has a material date.
cards.notes: Use a calendar. No notice uploads, reference numbers or incident detail. A date does not establish Provider capacity.

cards.prompt: What support do you need for this work?
options: Change Provider / take over existing work
cards.why: Separates continuity or transfer from a problem with the underlying work.
cards.when: The service branch needs an intent and it is not already clear.
cards.notes: Not sure is exclusive. Use across Tax/VAT, EPR, WEEE, batteries, filings and ongoing chemical services. Ask issue details only if an issue was selected.

cards.prompt: Anything not covered by these choices?
cards.why: Provides a limited escape route when a predefined option is missing.
cards.when: Optional, after a short predefined clarification or an unlisted company type.
cards.notes: Approved exception to selection-only: optional 2–3 sentences, proposed 500-character cap. Exclude personal, confidential or sensitive information. Suggest structured choices and require confirmation or correction before matching. Do not infer legal obligations. AI processing and privacy implementation remain open.

cards.prompt: Would you like a Provider to assess this need?
options: Find a Provider to assess this need
cards.why: Lets the user explicitly request advice when a detail remains unknown.
cards.when: At review, a relevant need is still unresolved after short clarification.
cards.notes: Not sure alone does not imply consent to an assessment. Match only a verified assessment service in the relevant jurisdiction; show a gap when unavailable.

cards.prompt: Review your request
cards.why: Lets the user correct the combined request and see any remaining uncertainty before Provider search.
cards.when: Once after all selected category branches.
cards.notes: Show selected services, country roles, product groups, current/planned facts, transfer intent, preferences and unresolved needs. Clear dependent answers when an upstream edit makes them irrelevant. Show coverage gaps rather than inventing matches.

groups.title: Tax/VAT
groups.purpose: Match the actual tax service, tax type and country, including ongoing support and Provider transfers.
notes: Use Tax/VAT in broad labels. Keep VAT/GST, sales tax, business income tax and payroll taxes as distinct actual tax types.
Bind registration status and work to each tax-country combination. Legal company form and tax election or status are separate.
Reuse the shared service-intent card for takeover or changing Provider. A routine transfer does not trigger issue questions.

cards.prompt: What Tax/VAT support do you need?
cards.why: Identifies the service before adding tax-specific details.
cards.when: Tax/VAT selected.

cards.prompt: Which countries do you need Tax/VAT support in?
options: Country selector: six regions on the same card; choose countries or territories without typing.
cards.why: Matches service jurisdiction rather than the first sales market.
cards.when: Requested service countries not confirmed.
cards.notes: Assign by tax or service inline if they differ.

cards.prompt: Which taxes do you need help with?
cards.why: Separates different tax specialisms without requiring technical tax codes.
cards.when: Ask only when relevant and not already confirmed for the same work.

cards.prompt: What is the registration status?
cards.why: Distinguishes initial registration, incomplete work and existing accounts.
cards.when: Registration status changes the selected work.
cards.mode: Choose one per tax and country
cards.notes: Different statuses opens the relevant tax-country rows inline.

cards.prompt: Which returns need support?
cards.why: Separates ordinary recurring filings from backlog or corrections.
cards.when: Returns selected.

cards.prompt: What kind of Tax/VAT issue is it?
cards.why: Finds relevant issue experience without collecting notices or financial data.
cards.when: Issue selected; not a routine takeover.

cards.prompt: What would you like reviewed?
cards.why: Matches advice to a concrete question.
cards.when: Review & advice selected and the purpose is not already clear.

cards.prompt: What needs updating?
cards.why: Distinguishes maintenance from closure and fresh registration.
cards.when: Update or close selected.

cards.prompt: Where do your employees work?
options: Country selector: six regions on the same card; choose countries or territories without typing.
cards.why: Captures employment locations, including remote work, independently of the company home country.
cards.when: Payroll support selected and work locations are unknown.
cards.notes: If no employees yet, ask planned work countries / Still deciding inline only when needed.

cards.prompt: What is the business structure?
cards.why: Routes income-tax support without treating a tax election as a legal form.
cards.when: Business income tax selected and structure is not already known.
cards.notes: Explain Company / LLC with relevant local examples such as corporation or limited company. Planned structure can be Still deciding. Do not list an S-corp election as a universal company form.

groups.title: EPR and Packaging with WEEE and Batteries
groups.purpose: Identify overlapping packaging, electronic-equipment and battery needs without asking users to know EPR categories.
notes: EPR means extended producer responsibility. A product can trigger more than one possible topic; a phone with a battery and packaging must not be forced into one exclusive category.
Use one joined intake. Preserve the existing destination IDs: packaging under product-packaging; WEEE and batteries under environment. Reuse shared product and battery facts.
Product descriptions and country choices screen possible services. A Provider confirms applicable duties, legal producer roles and local classifications.

cards.prompt: Which products do you sell or plan to sell?
cards.why: Separates electronics, standalone batteries and other products while allowing overlap.
cards.when: Product facts not already confirmed for this work.

cards.prompt: Do any of these products contain or come with batteries?
cards.why: Captures built-in batteries and batteries supplied with a product without adding another full wizard page.
cards.when: Inline with product choice for electronics or other physical products.
cards.notes: Skip repeat for standalone batteries. If only some groups, assign the fact inline to those groups.

cards.prompt: Which packaging activities apply?
cards.why: Describes actual packaging activity instead of the ambiguous category Packaged products.
cards.when: Packaging may be relevant.
cards.notes: No packaging and Not sure are each exclusive. Do not assume all sellers add packaging themselves.

cards.prompt: How are you involved with these products?
cards.why: Records the activity needed to assess local producer roles.
cards.when: Role facts are missing.
cards.notes: Assign by product group if different. Sourcing abroad does not by itself establish the legal importer role.

cards.prompt: Which countries do you need support in?
options: Country selector: six regions on the same card; choose countries or territories without typing.
cards.why: Connects each possible packaging, WEEE or battery need to the correct service jurisdiction.
cards.when: Not already confirmed for the exact topic.
cards.notes: Confirm common countries once or assign different countries by topic inline.

cards.prompt: What support do you need?
cards.why: Separates registration, recurring work, collection arrangements and representation.
cards.when: EPR, WEEE or battery topic selected.
cards.notes: Reuse the same service intent and takeover choices for all three topic families.

cards.prompt: What is the registration status?
cards.why: Keeps an existing battery registration separate from an unregistered packaging need.
cards.when: Status affects requested work.
cards.mode: Choose one per topic and country
cards.notes: Different statuses expands topic-country rows inline.

cards.prompt: What registration support do you need?
cards.why: Separates new work from maintenance and closure.
cards.when: Register, update or close selected.

cards.prompt: Which reporting or fee support do you need?
cards.why: Distinguishes ordinary reporting, backlog and calculation help without collecting weights.
cards.when: Reporting & fees selected.

cards.prompt: What kind of issue is it?
cards.why: Routes an issue to the relevant service specialist.
cards.when: Issue explicitly selected.

cards.prompt: What are the batteries used in?
cards.why: Finds battery expertise using familiar examples rather than asking users for legal battery classes.
cards.when: Battery support selected and this detail changes capability fit.
cards.notes: These are business descriptions. The Provider confirms the jurisdiction-specific category.

cards.prompt: Which electrical or electronic products are involved?
cards.why: Identifies the product experience needed for WEEE work.
cards.when: WEEE support selected and product groups are unknown.

cards.prompt: Which packaging materials are involved?
cards.why: Adds a packaging specialism only when it helps identify a Provider.
cards.when: Packaging service requires material detail; otherwise skip.

groups.title: Data and Privacy
groups.purpose: Route reviews, documents, ongoing work, individual requests and incidents while collecting only broad business context.
notes: Prioritise an incident, request or authority notice before general context. Ask only missing facts that affect the selected service.
The detailed sensitive-information checklist was withdrawn. Do not reintroduce health, biometric, criminal-record or other sensitive inventories in the normal journey.
Under 18 is a broad screening flag, not a universal legal age or consent threshold. Country and activity facts do not automatically determine the applicable privacy law.
The final Privacy Policy and the optional explanation processing arrangements remain launch dependencies. No actual records, breach details, names or correspondence are collected.

Confirm requested service countries inline using the approved country control when they are not already confirmed. People locations, business establishment and requested Provider jurisdiction are separate facts.

cards.prompt: What privacy support do you need?
cards.why: Separates distinct privacy services and puts active issues into a focused route.
cards.when: Data & Privacy selected.

cards.prompt: Whose personal information does your business handle?
options: People whose information we handle for clients
cards.why: Provides broad context for the selected task without collecting records about individuals.
cards.when: Only if it affects the service and is not already known.

cards.prompt: Does this include information about anyone under 18?
cards.why: Flags possible experience with children without asking for ages, names or legal conclusions.
cards.when: Inline with relevant people groups; only when material.
cards.notes: A screening flag only. The Provider assesses local age rules.

cards.prompt: Where are these people located?
options: Country selector: six regions on the same card; choose countries or territories without typing.
cards.why: Separates people locations from sales markets, company establishment and data storage.
cards.when: Needed to scope this privacy service.
cards.notes: Allow assignment by people group inline. Planned wording: Where will these people be located? Include Still deciding. Ask to confirm proposed reuse from sales markets.

cards.prompt: What do you use personal information for?
cards.why: Adds activity context that changes the privacy specialism required.
cards.when: Only if relevant to this selected privacy task.

cards.prompt: Who decides why and how the information is used?
cards.why: Helps identify advice for client processing or shared decisions without assigning a legal role.
cards.when: Client services or mixed arrangements make this material.
cards.notes: Do not automatically label controller, processor or joint controller. Multiple answers may apply to different activities.

cards.prompt: Which documents need support?
cards.why: Matches the document type rather than asking the user to upload it.
cards.when: Policies & agreements selected.

cards.prompt: What would you like done with these documents?
cards.why: Distinguishes drafting, professional review and updating, including documents initially drafted with AI.
cards.when: Policies & agreements; skip when the task is already clear.
cards.notes: Do not ask which AI tool wrote a policy. Assign actions to document types inline if needed. This is the final approved refinement.

cards.prompt: Which ongoing support do you need?
cards.why: Separates ongoing advice, officer support, maintenance and training.
cards.when: Ongoing privacy support selected.
cards.notes: DPO means data protection officer. Selecting this service does not establish that a statutory appointment is required.

cards.prompt: What needs a response?
cards.why: Finds experience with the relevant response process.
cards.when: Request, complaint or authority notice selected.
cards.notes: Helper: for example, a request to access, correct or delete information. No actual correspondence.

cards.prompt: What incident support do you need?
cards.why: Separates triage, response and later review without collecting sensitive incident narratives.
cards.when: Data breach or suspected incident selected.
cards.notes: Do not imply emergency capacity or a universal reporting deadline. Use the scoped deadline card only when relevant.

cards.prompt: What would you like reviewed?
cards.why: Identifies the advice topic while avoiding a detailed data inventory.
cards.when: Review & advice selected and purpose is not already clear.
cards.notes: Data storage, recipient and access locations are separate facts if a later approved specialist intake needs them; never infer them from sales countries.

groups.title: Marketing Compliance
groups.purpose: Separate marketing channels, claims, consent processes and search visibility so each request reaches the right specialist.
notes: Search & AI visibility is an approved service design, but its Provider service code and capability coverage still need implementation.
Claims about products belong here when used in marketing. Mandatory product labels, warnings and instructions belong under Product Compliance. Link overlapping work once.
SEO means search engine optimisation. GEO means optimisation for visibility in generative AI answers. Search-platform documentation supports technical design; it is not government regulation.

cards.prompt: What marketing support do you need?
cards.why: Separates different marketing compliance and visibility specialisms.
cards.when: Marketing Compliance selected.
cards.notes: Helper for SEO / GEO: being found in search engines and AI answers.

cards.prompt: What would you like a Provider to help with?
cards.why: Distinguishes advice, implementation, maintenance and an active issue.
cards.when: Action is not already clear.
cards.notes: Assign by topic inline if different; reuse existing service intent.

cards.prompt: Which countries do you need support in?
options: Country selector: six regions on the same card; choose countries or territories without typing.
cards.why: Scopes each marketing task to relevant markets.
cards.when: Service countries not confirmed.
cards.notes: Confirm common countries or assign by topic inline.

cards.prompt: Where do you need cookies or tracking support?
cards.why: Identifies the relevant technical environment.
cards.when: Cookies & tracking selected and environment is unknown.
cards.notes: Planned websites and apps count; reuse known channel facts.

cards.prompt: Which messaging channels need support?
cards.why: Separates channel-specific marketing rules and setup.
cards.when: Email / SMS marketing selected and channel is unknown.

cards.prompt: What needs checking?
cards.why: Finds the relevant review expertise without collecting campaign content.
cards.when: Advertising & product claims selected.
cards.notes: Product-claim examples: health, performance or environmental claims. Mandatory labels route to Product Compliance; do not ask the same shared claim need twice.

cards.prompt: Which activities need support?
cards.why: Separates distinct promotion and disclosure needs.
cards.when: Influencers, affiliates & reviews selected.

cards.prompt: Which consent or opt-out processes need support?
cards.why: Distinguishes collection from ongoing preference management.
cards.when: Consent & opt-out processes selected.
cards.notes: Reuse the same privacy or marketing work once, with linked category specialisms.

cards.prompt: What kind of marketing issue is it?
cards.why: Distinguishes regulator, claimant and platform response experience.
cards.when: Notice or issue selected.
cards.notes: Use scoped deadline where relevant; no notices or ad account identifiers.

cards.prompt: Where do you want better visibility?
cards.why: Separates search and AI visibility capability.
cards.when: Search & AI visibility selected.
cards.notes: Do not promise placement, ranking or inclusion in AI answers.

cards.prompt: Which content languages do you need help with?
options: Language selector: choose from the maintained language catalogue without typing.
cards.why: Matches language capability for the content itself.
cards.when: SEO / GEO work needs content-language expertise and it is unknown.
cards.notes: Keep separate from support communication languages. No URLs, keywords or ranking data in this wizard.

groups.title: Company Setup and Filings
groups.purpose: Match formation, additional registrations, ongoing administration, changes and closure using local company terminology.
notes: Use New company formation and Ongoing filings. Do not narrow all filings to annual filings.

Choose the country first, then a state or region only where relevant, then verified local company types on the same card. Names such as LLC, GmbH, SARL and BV are local forms, not universal equivalents.
Country-specific form catalogues remain incomplete. Verified examples are not a global production catalogue. More company types appears only when additional verified entries exist.
Need advice is an explicit service request. Not decided yet is a state and does not silently opt the user into advice.

cards.prompt: What company support do you need?
options: Register an existing company in another location
cards.why: Separates formation from expansion, administration, changes and closure.
cards.when: Company Setup & Filings selected.

cards.prompt: Where would you like to form your company?
options: Need advice on where to establish
cards.why: Separates a known location from an advice request and an undecided location.
cards.when: New company formation selected.
cards.notes: Choose location opens country, then state or region where needed, on this card. Advice can cover country, state or city as relevant; do not require a speculative location.

cards.prompt: Which company type do you need?
options: Verified local company types with short English descriptions
cards.why: Lets users select a familiar local form while preserving an unlisted or undecided state.
cards.when: Formation country is known; inline after location.
cards.notes: Options depend on the verified country/state catalogue. More appears only when further verified types exist. Unlisted opens the optional explanation and confirmed structured interpretation. Skip type if location advice is needed first.

cards.prompt: Where will you mainly run the business from?
options: Country selector: six regions on the same card; choose countries or territories without typing.
cards.why: Adds operating context when advice on formation location needs it.
cards.when: Location is undecided and this fact is needed and missing.
cards.notes: Do not infer the formation jurisdiction from operating base. Multiple countries expands country selection inline.

cards.prompt: Who will own the new company?
cards.why: Distinguishes owner types without asking for identities, names or ownership percentages.
cards.when: New company formation selected and it affects the requested service.
cards.notes: One individual can be an owner or shareholder; shareholder does not mean more than one person.

cards.prompt: Will any owners be based outside the formation country?
cards.why: Finds experience with foreign owners when the new formation country is known.
cards.when: New formation only; owner type and formation country are known.
cards.notes: For people, based means where they live; for companies, where registered. This is not an eligibility decision and is not a general branch-registration gate.

cards.prompt: Where do you need registration support?
options: Need advice on where to register
cards.why: Captures an additional registration in any country, including another location in the company home country.
cards.when: Register an existing company elsewhere selected.
cards.notes: Country and relevant state or region inline. Reuse an already registered location for ongoing support or a Provider change.

cards.prompt: What stage is the registration at?
cards.why: Routes unfinished registrations and ongoing support differently.
cards.when: Existing-company registration selected; skip advice-only request.
cards.notes: Already registered leads to support for that registration, rather than a forced new application.

cards.prompt: What needs changing?
cards.why: Identifies the change specialism without collecting company records.
cards.when: Update company details or structure selected.

cards.prompt: Which ongoing support do you need?
cards.why: Distinguishes recurring formal work and address or agent services.
cards.when: Company filings & ongoing support selected.
cards.notes: Company secretarial support means formal company administration, records and filings.

cards.prompt: What filing support do you need?
cards.why: Makes an ordinary transfer possible without implying a late or incorrect filing.
cards.when: Ongoing filings selected and intent is unknown.

cards.prompt: What filing issue needs support?
cards.why: Finds corrective filing expertise only when an issue exists.
cards.when: Resolve a filing issue selected.

cards.prompt: Which registered service do you need?
cards.why: Separates two services that require different local capabilities.
cards.when: Registered address or agent services selected.
cards.notes: Use verified local terminology and rules. Do not treat a registered address as a registered agent.

cards.prompt: What would you like to close?
cards.why: Separates company closure from ending one registration.
cards.when: Close a company selected.

cards.prompt: Is the company having difficulty paying its debts?
cards.why: Identifies possible debt or insolvency expertise for a closure request.
cards.when: Closing a company; skip branch-only closure.
cards.notes: No financial amounts. This question does not determine legal insolvency or eligibility for a closure procedure.

groups.title: Product Compliance
groups.purpose: Match service, product group and market, with short extra checks only for specialist products.
notes: Ask product facts before product-specific specialist questions. Reuse the same product group, battery and market facts from EPR or other branches.
Mandatory product information, warnings and instructions are here. Marketing claims link to Marketing Compliance. Intellectual property belongs under Legal Support.
Medical, food, cosmetic-claim, children’s-product and wireless flags are matching descriptions. A Provider confirms regulatory classification, approval requirements and applicable roles.

cards.prompt: What product compliance support do you need?
cards.why: Identifies the service without making users select a legal regime.
cards.when: Product Compliance selected.

cards.prompt: Which products need support?
cards.why: Finds the relevant product specialist using familiar groups.
cards.when: Product groups for this work are unknown.
cards.notes: More product types expands Household products or furniture; Chemicals or cleaning products; Machinery or industrial products; Medical or healthcare products; Other products. More is a disclosure control, not a stored product group.

cards.prompt: Which countries do these products need support in?
options: Country selector: six regions on the same card; choose countries or territories without typing.
cards.why: Connects product requirements and representation to the relevant market.
cards.when: Product service countries not confirmed.
cards.notes: Confirm common countries or assign by product group inline.

cards.prompt: How are you involved with these products?
cards.why: Records activity without requiring users to know their legal product role.
cards.when: Same-group activity not already confirmed.

cards.prompt: Are these products already being sold?
cards.why: Separates market-entry support from existing product compliance.
cards.when: Sales stage changes the work and is not known.
cards.notes: Some opens product-group rows inline. Preserve current and planned markets; do not assume all groups have the same stage.

cards.prompt: Which testing or approval support do you need?
cards.why: Separates technical assessment, testing delivery and approval work.
cards.when: Testing, certification & approvals selected.

cards.prompt: Which registration or document support do you need?
options: Change Provider / take over existing work
cards.why: Captures new work, maintenance, transfers and document review.
cards.when: Product registrations & compliance documents selected.

cards.prompt: What label or instruction support do you need?
options: Translate or adapt for another market
cards.why: Separates creation, review and market adaptation.
cards.when: Labels, warnings & instructions selected.
cards.notes: For translation or adaptation, select content languages inline. Reuse the same requested translation work once.

cards.prompt: What representative support do you need?
cards.why: Distinguishes advice, appointment, transfer and review.
cards.when: Responsible person / local representative selected.
cards.notes: Verify the exact role for the product and country. A generic representative service does not prove GPSR, medical, EPR or chemical representative capability.

cards.prompt: What kind of product issue is it?
cards.why: Finds issue and recall expertise without deciding that a recall is legally required.
cards.when: Product issue, notice or recall selected.
cards.notes: Prioritise the focused issue route and a relevant deadline. Do not request incident reports, identities or documents.

cards.prompt: What would you like reviewed?
cards.why: Scopes advice without repeating an already clear purpose.
cards.when: Review & advice selected and purpose is unknown.

cards.prompt: Which medical or healthcare products are involved?
cards.why: Avoids matching all healthcare products to one generic product specialist.
cards.when: Medical or healthcare group selected and subtype changes fit.
cards.notes: Descriptions are not legal classifications; protective equipment and software may need separate assessments.

cards.prompt: Which food or feed products are involved?
cards.why: Separates food, supplements, specialist nutrition and animal feed expertise.
cards.when: Food, drinks or supplements selected and subtype changes fit.
cards.notes: Specialist nutrition includes products for particular medical dietary needs; classification remains for the Provider.

cards.prompt: Do any selected products make these claims?
cards.why: Flags claims that can affect which cosmetic or healthcare specialist is needed.
cards.when: Cosmetics or personal care selected and this affects fit.
cards.notes: Neither and Not sure are exclusive. Examples of conditions: acne or dandruff. Do not automatically classify the product as a medicine.

cards.prompt: Which children’s products are involved?
cards.why: Separates toys from other products intended for children.
cards.when: Toys or children’s products selected and subtype changes fit.

cards.prompt: Do any of these products have wireless or radio functions?
cards.why: Finds radio-equipment expertise for relevant electronic, toy or medical products.
cards.when: Relevant product group and feature not already confirmed.
cards.notes: Examples: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth or mobile connectivity. If yes, assign to product groups inline. No radio frequencies or device identifiers.

groups.title: Logistics and Customs
groups.purpose: Match paired routes, logistics services, transport modes and handling needs without asking users to classify dangerous goods themselves.
notes: Preserve each departure-destination pair. Shipping departure country, manufacturing origin and stock location are different facts.
Use Recurring shipments and Ground. Ground maps to road/truck capability internally; Rail stays a separate option.
Selecting all applicable modes is possible. Need advice on transport is exclusive; an All above option does not replace unknown or advice states.

cards.prompt: What logistics or customs support do you need?
cards.why: Separates customs, transport and warehouse capabilities.
cards.when: Logistics & Customs selected.
cards.notes: Helper for duties: customs charges, product codes and origin rules.

cards.prompt: Where are the goods moving from and to?
cards.why: Matches actual route coverage without merging unrelated departure and destination countries.
cards.when: Clearance, freight, route advice or shipment issue selected.
cards.notes: Use the country selector at each end. Add another route repeats the pair inline. Planned routes count. Warehouse-only work skips this.

cards.prompt: Is this for a one-off shipment or recurring shipments?
cards.why: Finds capacity for a single job and continuing operations.
cards.when: Customs clearance or shipping selected and recurrence is unknown.

cards.prompt: What kind of shipping do you need?
cards.why: Separates parcel networks from pallet, container and bulk transport.
cards.when: Shipping selected and type is unknown.
cards.notes: Helper: freight includes pallets, containers or bulk goods.

cards.prompt: Which transport modes do you need?
cards.why: Matches transport capabilities while supporting journeys using several modes.
cards.when: Freight selected and modes are unknown.
cards.notes: Need advice is exclusive. Ground means road/truck in internal capability mapping; Rail remains separate.

cards.prompt: Which warehouse or fulfilment services do you need?
cards.why: Separates storage from picking, packing, dispatch and marketplace preparation.
cards.when: Warehousing / fulfilment selected.
cards.notes: Explain fulfilment as picking, packing and dispatching orders; marketplace preparation as preparing goods for marketplace fulfilment centres.

cards.prompt: Where do you need warehouse or fulfilment support?
options: Country selector: six regions on the same card; choose countries or territories without typing.
cards.why: Matches the actual warehouse service location.
cards.when: Warehouse or fulfilment selected and requested location is unknown.
cards.notes: City or area selector only where needed for availability. Offer known stock countries for confirmation; do not assume they are the requested new locations.

cards.prompt: Do the goods need any of this handling?
cards.why: Finds handling expertise without requiring dangerous-goods classification.
cards.when: Shipping or storage work needs handling capability.
cards.notes: None of these and Not sure are exclusive. Reuse battery facts. Provider confirms transport classification; no UN numbers or technical packing data.

cards.prompt: Where do you need customs clearance support?
cards.why: Separates export and import clearance capabilities on each route.
cards.when: Customs clearance selected.
cards.notes: Display actual paired route countries. Confirm common answer or assign by route inline.

cards.prompt: Which duties or classification topics need support?
cards.why: Separates classification, valuation, origin and relief expertise.
cards.when: Duties, product classification or origin selected.
cards.notes: Do not ask for actual product codes, values or origin proofs.

cards.prompt: Which import or export topics need support?
cards.why: Matches the advice or local role needed for the route.
cards.when: Import / export review & advice selected.
cards.notes: Verify actual local role capability. Do not promise a universally valid importer-of-record or exporter service.

cards.prompt: What kind of shipment or customs issue is it?
cards.why: Finds relevant response expertise without collecting shipment identifiers or paperwork.
cards.when: Shipment or customs issue selected.
cards.notes: Reuse route and product facts; scoped deadline only where relevant.

groups.title: Legal Support
groups.purpose: Route business legal work by topic, country, action and matter stage, including specialist IP and notary services.
notes: Business and professional work only until the personal-user scope decision is resolved. Individual employee claims remain a separate open decision.
Legal Support has no seeded subcategories in the compatibility inventory. IP, notary and other specialist services require explicit service records and verified Provider capability.
Requested country, governing law, forum, property location, document origin, document use and appointment location are distinct. The Provider confirms professional authority and jurisdiction.
Online communication preference does not establish the availability or validity of an online notarial act.

cards.prompt: What legal support do you need?
cards.why: Separates distinct legal specialisms rather than matching a general parent label.
cards.when: Legal Support selected.

cards.prompt: Which countries do you need legal support in?
options: Country selector: six regions on the same card; choose countries or territories without typing.
cards.why: Identifies requested service coverage without guessing governing law.
cards.when: Legal service jurisdictions are not already confirmed.
cards.notes: State, province or region selector only where material. Assign by legal topic inline when different. Provider confirms governing law and forum.

cards.prompt: What would you like a Provider to do?
options: Help with a dispute or proceeding
Change Provider / take over existing work
cards.why: Separates advice, documents, applications, disputes and a transfer.
cards.when: Action is not already clear.
cards.notes: Show relevant actions only for the selected topic; reuse the same matter action.

cards.prompt: Which intellectual property needs support?
cards.why: Matches the specific IP practice rather than treating all IP rights as trademarks.
cards.when: Trademarks & intellectual property selected.
cards.notes: No brand names, inventions, code or confidential details in the wizard.

cards.prompt: What stage is the IP application or right at?
cards.why: Distinguishes application, prosecution and maintenance work.
cards.when: An application or registration service is relevant.
cards.mode: Choose one per right and country
cards.notes: Different stages opens rows inline. Do not assume registration or validity in another jurisdiction.

cards.prompt: Which contracts or agreements need support?
cards.why: Finds the relevant drafting and review experience.
cards.when: Contracts & agreements selected.
cards.notes: Reuse action already chosen. Link privacy agreements or other overlapping work once.

cards.prompt: Which workplace topics need support?
cards.why: Routes business-side employment work to a suitable specialist.
cards.when: Employment / workplace selected.
cards.notes: Use employee work countries, not company registration country. Individual employee claims remain on hold pending scope decision.

cards.prompt: What stage is the dispute at?
cards.why: Matches the current matter stage without imposing a fixed sequence.
cards.when: Dispute or proceeding selected.
cards.notes: No steps taken yet and Not sure are each exclusive. No claim amounts, allegations, parties or case numbers.

cards.prompt: What do you need help doing?
cards.why: Distinguishes bringing a claim from defending or responding to one.
cards.when: A dispute or claim needs this detail.
cards.notes: Both can include a counterclaim. Reuse for the same IP, contract, employment or property matter. It does not automatically mean court proceedings.

cards.prompt: Which company legal work needs support?
cards.why: Separates transaction and governance experience.
cards.when: Company transactions or ownership selected.

cards.prompt: Which commercial property work needs support?
cards.why: Finds relevant commercial property expertise.
cards.when: Commercial property or leases selected.
cards.notes: Select property country and relevant state/city when needed for the service. No street address or price.

cards.prompt: Which regulatory support do you need?
cards.why: Separates advice, applications and enforcement work.
cards.when: Regulatory advice or authority notices selected.
cards.notes: Reuse known tax, product, privacy or other subject. If missing, use a short topic clarification. No typed regulator name or notice upload.

cards.prompt: Which notary or authentication services do you need?
cards.why: Distinguishes notarial acts and cross-border authentication support.
cards.when: Notary services & document authentication selected.
cards.notes: Explain formal company or property notarial work where relevant. Verify local availability and authority; not all lawyers are notaries and not all notaries provide legal advice.

cards.prompt: Where are the documents from and where will they be used?
cards.why: Keeps origin-use relationships intact for authentication advice.
cards.when: Apostille or legalisation support selected.
cards.notes: Origin means the issuing authority or notary country. Add each document group inline. Do not conclude that an Apostille is required or sufficient from these answers alone.

cards.prompt: How would you prefer the notary appointment?
cards.why: Distinguishes appointment preference from legal eligibility for a remote act.
cards.when: An appointment-based notary service selected.
cards.notes: In person opens requested appointment country and relevant city/area / Not sure. Online availability and receiving-country acceptance must be confirmed by a qualified Provider.

cards.prompt: Where will the person signing be located during the online appointment?
options: Country selector: six regions on the same card; choose countries or territories without typing.
cards.why: Identifies signer-location restrictions independently of document origin, use or company location.
cards.when: Online notary appointment requested and a signing act is involved.
cards.notes: Allow multiple countries for different signers. State or region only where needed. Unknown keeps online completion unconfirmed. No identities or identity documents.

groups.title: Environmental Chemical and Substance Compliance
groups.purpose: Identify chemical, mixture and article activities, then match the requested specialist service without collecting formulas or dossiers.
notes: Ask or reuse the product/material group first, then countries, then the service. Add activity context only where it changes matching.
WEEE and batteries reuse the joined EPR journey and keep the existing environment destination. Do not repeat those product, status or takeover questions.
Broad manufacture, import and sale descriptions do not determine a legal chemical role. Representative roles and substance regimes require jurisdiction-specific verification.
The approved chemical journey does not create a supported catalogue for general ESG, emissions, site permits or every environmental service.

cards.prompt: Which products or materials need support?
cards.why: Separates chemical production, formulated mixtures and finished-product work.
cards.when: Chemical or substance support selected; same-group facts unknown.
cards.notes: Formulated examples: cleaners, paints and adhesives. Finished products open the existing product-family selector. Reuse known product groups.

cards.prompt: Which countries do you need support in?
options: Country selector: six regions on the same card; choose countries or territories without typing.
cards.why: Connects the actual chemical service to the relevant production, import, supply or use country.
cards.when: After products/materials; service countries not confirmed.
cards.notes: Confirm common countries or assign by product/material group inline. Do not require unrelated countries.

cards.prompt: What chemical or substance support do you need?
cards.why: Separates the specialist service without requiring chemical identifiers.
cards.when: After relevant product/material and country context.

cards.prompt: How are you involved with these products or materials?
cards.why: Distinguishes actual activities that can require different chemical expertise.
cards.when: Only when activity changes the requested service.
cards.notes: General manufacturing is not automatically manufacture of a chemical substance under a particular law.

cards.prompt: Which registration or notification support do you need?
options: Change Provider / take over existing work
cards.why: Separates new work, unfinished work, maintenance and transfers.
cards.when: Registrations or notifications selected.

cards.prompt: Which restriction or product checks do you need?
cards.why: Finds assessment, documentation and testing capability.
cards.when: Substance restrictions or product checks selected.
cards.notes: Reuse product testing work once; retain the additional chemical specialism.

cards.prompt: Which materials need support?
cards.why: Separates the two document types without collecting their contents.
cards.when: Safety data sheets / hazard labels selected.
cards.notes: SDS means safety data sheet. This card asks about document types, not ingredients.

cards.prompt: What safety data sheet or hazard-label support do you need?
options: Translate or adapt for another market
cards.why: Matches creation, technical review and market adaptation.
cards.when: Inline with the document-type choice; action is unknown.
cards.notes: For translation, select content languages inline. A general label or translation capability is not enough without verified chemical expertise.

cards.prompt: What local representative support do you need?
cards.why: Separates advice, appointment, transfer and review.
cards.when: Local representative selected.
cards.notes: Match the exact chemical role and country, such as a REACH Only Representative where relevant. Do not substitute a generic product representative.

cards.prompt: Which ongoing support do you need?
options: Safety data sheet or label updates
Monitor rule changes or ongoing advice
cards.why: Finds maintenance and advisory capability without repeating initial-registration questions.
cards.when: Ongoing reporting or updates selected.
cards.notes: Reuse the takeover intent card if changing Provider. A takeover is not automatically an issue.

cards.prompt: What kind of chemical or substance issue is it?
cards.why: Finds response expertise without collecting technical dossiers or notices.
cards.when: Authority notice or issue selected.
cards.notes: Link the same product, customs or legal issue once. Use scoped deadline only where relevant.

cards.prompt: What would you like reviewed?
options: New or changed product or material
cards.why: Scopes advice to the actual business change or uncertainty.
cards.when: Review & advice selected and purpose unknown.
